problem:
Compute the variance ${\sigma }^{2}$ of a data set ${x}_{i}$ consisting of $8$ data points, where

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}=-112,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2}=1736.
$$

${\sigma }^{2}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=8$ points in our data set, and we know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}=-112,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot (-112) \\  & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ We know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2}=1736,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 1736 \\  & =217.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =217-{(-14)}^{2} \\  & =217-196 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$
